collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager borrowing a friend's hut finds everything slightly wrong, even a staring owl: turn the owl round, or get used to it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s roof is being rethatched, so (subject.he/she) is sleeping in (friend)'s hut for a few nights while (friend) stays with family. Everything in it is very slightly wrong. The water jar is on the wrong side. The mat faces the wrong way. There is a carved owl on a shelf that seems to be looking directly at (subject.him/her) wherever (subject.he/she) goes.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) turns the owl to face the wall. Better. On the last morning, before giving the hut back, (subject.he/she) turns it round again and puts everything back exactly as it was. (friend) comes home and immediately says, "You turned the owl." (subject) has no idea how (friend.he/she) knew.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) decides to live like (friend) for a few nights: water jar on the left, mat facing the door, the owl watching. By the third night (subject.he/she) quite likes it. When (subject.he/she) goes home to (subject.his/her) own hut, (subject.he/she) moves the water jar to the left. (subject.He/she) never moves it back.
